summary: Initial security intake focused on whether NimbusWorks can use Redwood Hosted versus Dedicated or Private. Key topics: SOC2/ISO posture, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs and retention, customer-managed KMS, encryption in transit/at rest, EU data residency. Nimbus prefers private or VPC-hosted for sensitive PII but is open to a Dedicated pilot if perf/cost checks out.
topics: Hosting options: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private/VPC
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Maya from Redwood. Uh, we'll run through a quick intake on security and hosting. Is this still a good time?
[00:12] Lena Ortiz: Yep good, thanks. We just have Markus and Priya and I on the call. We wanted to understand where Redwood sits on certs and, uh, encryption.
[00:22] Jordan Patel: Cool. Quick intros, Jordan from Redwood SE — I work on private deployments and networking. Samir is on for sizing questions after.
[00:30] Markus Feld: Quick context: NimbusWorks handles EU customer PII for payroll, so SOC2 + ISO are baseline, and we have strict log retention controls. We're evaluating whether we go hosted or have Redwood run in our VPC.
[00:45] Maya Chen: Understood. At a high level we offer three deployment modes: Hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private (VPC or on-prem). For regulated PII you mentioned, many customers start with Dedicated or Private.
[00:58] Priya Rao: Can you confirm SOC2 Type II and any ISO certs? I've seen your compliance page but need the artifacts.
[01:09] Maya Chen: Yes, we are SOC2 Type II — I will share the report. For ISO we hold ISO 27001 scoping for the platform, and we have an internal audit summary. I'll attach both.
[01:22] Lena Ortiz: Great. About identity — we use SAML-based SSO with SCIM provisioning. We need team-level RBAC with separation for dev vs prod, and auditability of admin actions.
[01:34] Jordan Patel: We support SSO via SAML and also OIDC — SCIM for user provisioning is supported. RBAC maps to org/space/route level; you can create roles like admin, dev, viewer. One thing to note: our audit logs capture API key rotations, user changes, model deployments and, uh, route-level access.
[01:54] Markus Feld: How long do you retain logs by default, and can we set retention to 7 years for audit trails?
[02:04] Maya Chen: Default retention in Hosted is 90 days for detailed request logs; longer retention is an add-on (we can retain for a year or more). In Private/VPC you control retention — we can wire logs to your SIEM (Splunk/Datadog) or to an S3 bucket you manage. For seven years we'd recommend Private + customer-managed storage.
[02:26] Priya Rao: That matches what we thought. KMS — can we use our own keys (bring-your-own-key)? We need HSM-backed KMS for at-rest encryption.
[02:36] Jordan Patel: Yes, Dedicated and Private support customer-managed keys. For Hosted there is an option for BYOK via our KMS integrations but that depends on contract and we often put a CMK in the customer's cloud account for VPC setups. HSM integration is supported in Private.
[02:52] Lena Ortiz: Okay. A bit more around network: when you say VPC, is that a private control plane or fully customer-controlled egress? We need no egress except to approved endpoints.
[03:05] Samir Rao: In our Private VPC deployment the control plane sits in Redwood-managed control, but data plane can be placed into your VPC. Egress is restricted — you can configure egress rules and NAT to approved destinations only. For air-gapped on-prem, we also offer an offline package.
[03:25] Markus Feld: Good. On the topic of model artifacts, do you store prompts or only the outputs? We have to ensure minimal data retention for customer content.
[03:36] Jordan Patel: By default, we store request/response traces for debugging and quality monitoring for a configurable window. For privacy-sensitive customers we can disable request logging and only keep aggregated telemetry. In Dedicated/Private you control what gets persisted. There was a comment — sorry, I said kayvee cache earlier, I meant KV cache — sometimes the auto transcript swaps words.
[03:58] Lena Ortiz: ha — thanks for clarifying. Do you have fine-grained controls for developers versus ops? We want devs to be able to run test prompts but not see production keys or raw PII.
[04:12] Maya Chen: Yep, RBAC can lock down routes and token scopes. We also support token-level scoping so you can issue short-lived tokens for dev sandboxing. We recommend separate projects/environments in the console.
[04:27] Priya Rao: What about encryption in transit? TLS only, or mTLS?
[04:33] Jordan Patel: TLS 1.2+ by default. For Private deployments we can enable mTLS between data plane components and customer infra; we also support mutual TLS for internal service-to-service calls when requested.
[04:46] Markus Feld: Are there pen tests or vulnerability scans you share?
[04:50] Maya Chen: We do quarterly pentests and internal code scans. We share summary findings and remediation timelines under an NDA.
[04:57] Lena Ortiz: One of our blockers is legal review — we need contract language about subprocessing and data residency. Do you have standard clauses?
[05:06] Maya Chen: Yes, we have a Data Processing Addendum (DPA) and standard subprocessor list. I'll include a copy. For residency, Dedicated or Private is the path — Hosted can be region-restricted but still involves Redwood-managed storage.
[05:22] Priya Rao: Pricing and SLAs: does Dedicated come with an SLA for latency and uptime?
[05:27] Samir Rao: Dedicated has SLA tiers depending on commit. We offer latency SLOs and uptime guarantees with penalties at enterprise tiers. For latency-sensitive inference we recommend reserved GPU pools and autoscaling settings we'll propose in a sizing doc.
[05:43] Markus Feld: Are model weights ever shared across tenants in Hosted? We need strong isolation.
[05:48] Jordan Patel: In Hosted, multi-tenant serving can share infrastructure but we enforce logical isolation and namespace separation; no model weights or customer data is shared. For absolute separation we recommend Dedicated or Private.
[06:02] Lena Ortiz: Can you walk through the audit log schema briefly? What fields are included?
[06:08] Jordan Patel: Sure — timestamp, actor, action (API call, deployment, key rotation), route/id, request id, truncated prompt hash (not full content unless requested), response metadata, and user agent/source IP. We can forward raw logs to your SIEM if you prefer.
[06:30] Priya Rao: About the truncated prompt hash — is that enough for us for forensics? We need the ability to reconstruct incidents.
[06:38] Maya Chen: For forensics we can enable full request logging in a controlled way and stream it into your own S3 with encryption and retention rules. That's the recommended pattern for when customers need long-term incident archives.
[06:54] Markus Feld: Regulatory note: we have to ensure EU PII never leaves EU. Is there an EU-only Private deployment option?
[07:02] Jordan Patel: Yes, we support region-constrained Private deployments in EU zones with data plane placed in customer VPC in EU. Hosted API in EU regions is possible but the control plane may be outside; for strict residency, Private is the safest route.
[07:19] Lena Ortiz: How about access reviews / certs for our admins? We need monthly attestations and an audit trail.
[07:25] Maya Chen: We support activity logs and a user provisioning model via SCIM so you can automate deprovisioning. Monthly attestation can be supported by exporting logs.
[07:37] Priya Rao: There was a mention earlier of a performance benchmark. For our use case we have real-time payroll risk scoring — latency budget is 120ms p95 for 512 token-ish sequences. Can Redwood meet that?
[07:51] Samir Rao: We'll propose a benchmark across hosted vs dedicated with model variants. Some customers achieve p95 ~80-150ms on dedicated setups; hosted can be lower-latency for small bursts but Dedicated gives predictability. We'll size the cluster to meet 120ms p95 target and show token-cost tradeoffs.
[08:12] Markus Feld: For the PII ingestion pipeline, are there pre-ingest transformations or redaction hooks?
[08:19] Jordan Patel: We support pre-request hooks where you can run redaction or tokenization in your environment before sending. In Private, you can keep redaction code inside the VPC so raw PII never leaves.
[08:35] Lena Ortiz: Any gotchas around backups or snapshots that might copy data out?
[08:41] Maya Chen: Backups are encrypted and for Private can be kept in your account. For Hosted, backups are managed by Redwood; we can add contractual restrictions on cross-region replication. We'll detail this in the data handling doc.
[08:57] Priya Rao: Ok, security team will want the full artifact pack and a short tech Q&A — can we schedule a follow-up focused on infra/network with your SEs?
[09:07] Maya Chen: Absolutely. Jordan and Samir can run a deep network + perf session. Do you have preferred times next week?
[09:13] Lena Ortiz: Mid-week is best, timezone is CET for us.
[09:17] Maya Chen: We'll propose slots in CET and include the benchmark plan and network diagram in the invite.
[09:25] Markus Feld: One last question: what's your default token scoping and are there any policy primitives to prevent exfil via model outputs?
[09:34] Jordan Patel: Token scoping can limit which models and routes tokens have access to; we also have content filtering policies and allowlist/denylist hooks. For exfil prevention we recommend a combination of output filters and restricting models that have access to customer data. In Private you can enforce stricter policy enforcement points.
[09:56] Priya Rao: Thanks. We'll also want to see any prior SOC2 remediation items that impact our controls.
[10:02] Maya Chen: I'll include the remediation summary under NDA.
[10:08] Lena Ortiz: Recap for our side: review artifacts, confirm data residency, schedule perf + network deep dive, and see Dedicated sizing.
[10:18] Maya Chen: Recap from Redwood: we'll send SOC2/ISO artifacts, DPA, network diagram, and a proposed benchmark/sizing doc. Jordan will own the perf plan.
[10:29] Samir Rao: I'll include example autoscaling settings and proposed GPU types.
[10:34] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up in the next 48 hours with artifacts and a Doodle for the deep dive.
[10:41] Lena Ortiz: Great, thanks. Bye all.
[10:43] [call ends]
notes: Reference artifacts to be attached: SOC2 Type II PDF, ISO audit summary, DPA and subprocessor list (link to shared drive), network diagram (VPC/private plan), Dedicated sizing spreadsheet, benchmark plan. Customer asked for EU-only data plane and 7-year retention for audit trails as a blocker to Hosted.
